::: {.why}
The fourth factor and the literature that followed it are the field's own replication crisis, arriving about a decade after the one you lived through in genetics.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Describe the Carhart momentum factor's construction and the one detail that makes it different from the other three.
- State the replication failure rate reported in the anomalies literature and give two competing explanations for post-publication decay.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>65 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [35 min]{.task-min} Read the Hou, Xue and Zhang abstract and results summary, and the McLean and Pontiff draft's abstract and its estimate of post-publication decay. The two papers make different claims and both are relevant: one says many were never real, the other says some were real and then got arbitraged.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [20 min]{.task-min} Measure the decay yourself on one factor: split the momentum factor's history at its publication year and report the Sharpe before and after, with an interval on each. Then do the same for value. The intervals will be wide, which is itself the finding.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [10 min]{.task-min} Write two sentences distinguishing the two explanations, and one on what evidence would separate them.
:::
:::
